meanings.note: Prefix 'за-' marks beginning an action, covering, or stopping by along the way (stem 'вязывать'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'would quit / wrap up'.

examples.text: Завязывал бы ты с картами, играть не умеешь.
examples.trans: You should quit cards, you do not know how to play.

examples.text: Надо всё сделать и завязывать вовремя.
examples.trans: We need to do everything and would quit on time.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian discourse particle adding conversational nuance meaning 'would', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Рыба дорогая, должна быть в идеальном состоянии.
examples.trans: The fish is expensive, it must be in perfect condition.

examples.text: Виктор Петрович, мне бы не хотелось, чтобы Элеонора Андреевна узнала.
examples.trans: Victor Petrovich, I would not want Eleonora Andreyevna to find out.

examples.text: Ну что, доча, обыграем дядю Мишу?
examples.trans: Well then, daughter, shall we beat Uncle Misha?

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'you (informal)', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Я не собираюсь перед тобой отчитываться.

examples.text: Масло оливковое, две бутылки.

meanings.note: Prefix 'у-' marks departure, removal, or successful completion (stem 'меть'). Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'know how, can', paired with 'суметь'.

examples.text: Я не умею.

meanings.note: Prefix 'по-' forms perfective verbs or marks a brief/onset action (stem 'тренироваться'). Reflexive/intransitive verb with the postfix '-ся'/'-сь' (historically from the reflexive pronoun 'себя', oneself). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'practice'.

examples.text: Надо всё сделать и потренироваться вовремя.
examples.trans: We need to do everything and practice on time.

examples.text: На нашей кухне все умеют потренироваться.
examples.trans: In our kitchen everyone knows how to practice.

meanings.note: Common feminine noun meaning 'arm' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: Руку убрал!

examples.text: Виктор Петрович, я прошу у вас руки вашей дочери.

examples.text: Далее судьба нашей рыбы попала в руки Айнуры.

meanings.note: Prefix 'под-' ('under, up to') indicates approaching or supporting from below (stem 'польный'). Adjective formed with the common Slavic suffix '-н-' from a noun/verb root. Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('underground / secret').

meanings.note: From Latin 'doctor' (teacher, scholar, from 'docere', to teach).

meanings.note: Relational adjective formed with the Slavic suffix '-ский' ('pertaining to'). Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('psychological').

examples.text: Доктор психологических наук.
examples.trans: Doctor of psychological sciences.

examples.text: Шеф говорит, что это очень психологический выбор.

examples.text: Доченька, поговори, пожалуйста, с доктором, он тебе поможет.

meanings.en: to have a talk, to speak (with someone)

examples.text: Доченька, поговори, пожалуйста, с доктором, он тебе поможет.

meanings.en: to be patient for a little while, to hold on
